LESSON: SCHOOL AND COMMUNITY

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: School and Community

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on School and Community. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can the school collaborate with the community?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify ways in which the school collaborates with the community
2. explain the benefits of collaboration between school and the community
3. appreciate the benefits of collaboration between the school and community

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SCHOOL AND COMMUNITY
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
School and Community helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: SCHOOL AND COMMUNITY
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify ways in which the school collaborates with the community

What this means
In this part you learn to identify ways in which the school collaborates with the community. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify ways in which the school collaborates with the community.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “School and Community” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify ways in which the school collaborates with the community. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the benefits of collaboration between school and the community

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the benefits of collaboration between school and the community. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the benefits of collaboration between school and the community.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to School and Community.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the benefits of collaboration between school and the community. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the benefits of collaboration between the school and community

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the benefits of collaboration between the school and community. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the benefits of collaboration between the school and community.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the benefits of collaboration between the school and community. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what School and Community is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “School and Community” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify ways in which the school collaborates with the community)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to School and Community. (skill: explain the benefits of collaboration between school and the community)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: appreciate the benefits of collaboration between the school and community)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach School and Community to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify ways in which the school collaborates with the community.
3. Practise this skill: explain the benefits of collaboration between school and the community.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the benefits of collaboration between the school and community.
5. Make one local Kenya example of School and Community from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for School and Community: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study School and Community?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can the school collaborate with the community?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what School and Community means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify ways in which the school collaborates with the community.
5. Be able to: explain the benefits of collaboration between school and the community.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
